filter.dateField: Which date to filter and sort by
filter.invalidLocalDate: That date does not exist in the selected timezone. The filter was cleared.

org.title: Organize library
org.subtitle: Move your media into a folder you choose, named by capture date. Dry-run first, undo any batch.
org.rootsHint: One destination folder per drive - any name, any location. Files stay on their own drive (instant rename, no copying).
org.noRoots: Pick a library folder to get started.
org.templateHint: Folder layout and file names are templates - change them to anything you like.
org.tokensHint: Date/time tokens come from the photo's capture date. {hash4} {hash8} {hash16} = first 4/8/16 characters of the file's content fingerprint (keeps identical names apart). {camera} = camera model from EXIF, e.g. "Apple iPhone 12" - left empty when the file has none. {relpath} = the file's original subfolders under its watched folder (keeps your manual sorting, e.g. "Bac Tuan\Tet 2008"); {folder} = just the closest folder name; both are folder-template only. {name} = the original file name without extension.
org.noHashTokenHint: Without a {hash4}/{hash8}/{hash16} token, Organize cannot tell two files apart by content: a second import of the same photos lands as _2 copies instead of being reported as duplicates. Use Dedup afterwards to clean them up.
org.includeUncertain: Also organize files with uncertain dates (file-time only)
org.previewInvalidated: The library changed, so the previous preview was cleared.
org.hashConfirm: Read the files that need content fingerprints? Live Photo items can include a paired video. This may take a while, runs as a cancellable background job, and must finish before a new preview.
org.hashRequired: Content fingerprint required - prepare hashes, then preview again
org.hashPreparedDone: Content fingerprints prepared. Run Preview again.
org.confirm: Move {{n}} files into your library folders? Every move is journaled and can be undone.
org.running: Busy - a scan/meta/fingerprint/organize job is running, wait for it to finish…
org.missingRoots: Drives without a library folder yet: {{drives}}
org.undoConfirm: Move {{n}} files back to where they were? Files whose target changed since are skipped and reported.

dedup.empty: No duplicates found. Hit "Scan for duplicates" after indexing.
dedup.pickGroup: Pick a group on the left. Checked cards get deleted, the rest stay.
dedup.confirm: Move {{n}} files ({{size}}) to the Recycle Bin? A Live Photo video moves only when the kept photo has a verified identical video. At least one verified copy of each photo always stays.
dedup.deleteResult: Moved {{n}} files to Recycle Bin ({{size}} freed)

reason.NO_RECYCLE_BIN: {{n}} on a drive without a Recycle Bin (external/FAT32) - delete those manually
reason.TRASH_FAILED: {{n}} failed to move to the Recycle Bin
reason.KEEP_NONE: {{n}} blocked: a whole group can never be deleted
reason.HASH_MISMATCH: {{n}} whose content doesn't match the kept copy
reason.CHANGED_ON_DISK: {{n}} changed on disk since hashing - rescan and retry
reason.SURVIVOR_CHANGED: {{n}} skipped because the kept copy changed on disk
reason.NOT_IN_GROUP: {{n}} not part of any duplicate group

dedup.keepGuard: At least one copy must stay in every group
dedup.markGroup: Mark the extra copies of this group (Shift+click for a range)
dedup.keys: Checkbox: mark for deletion · Shift+click: range · Ctrl+A / Ctrl+D: mark / clear all · Del: delete marked · Space, 1-9, arrows, Enter: within a group
dedup.kindExactHint: Byte-for-byte identical (BLAKE3 match) - deleting the extras is completely safe
dedup.kindSimilarHint: Same photo, different bytes: re-compressed, resized, exported by another app. The copies are NOT identical, so look before you delete.
dedup.emptySimilar: No similar photos yet. Hit "Scan for similar photos" - it's quick when thumbnails are already cached.
dedup.confirmSimilar:
Move {{n}} files ({{size}}) to the Recycle Bin?

These are SIMILAR, not identical: the copies may differ in resolution and compression. The app only guarantees that every group keeps at least one copy and that the kept copy is still intact on disk - judging which one to keep is up to you.
